LRU Cache with Time-To-Live (TTL) Expiry and Thread Safety

This module implements a high-performance, thread-safe Least Recently Used (LRU)
cache that supports Time-To-Live (TTL) expiration for cached items. It is designed
for use in concurrent environments where data freshness and memory limits are critical.

Key Features:
1. LRU Eviction: When the cache reaches its maximum size, the least recently used
   item is evicted to make room for new entries.
2. TTL Expiry: Each cached item can have an associated Time-To-Live (in seconds).
   Once an item's TTL expires, it is considered invalid and will be evicted either
   lazily (on access) or eagerly (during maintenance sweeps).
3. Thread Safety: All public methods are protected by fine-grained locking to
   ensure thread safety without sacrificing too much performance.
4. Lazy and Eager Expiration: Expired items are removed on access (lazy) and
   optionally during background maintenance sweeps (eager).
5. Callbacks: Supports custom callbacks for eviction and expiration events.

- We use a doubly linked list combined with a hash map (dictionary) for O(1)
